stories.title: Dublin traffic restrictions under way ahead of EU summits
stories.summary: Part of Dublin city's North Wall Quay is closed to traffic as restrictions begin ahead of two major summits being held this week. A major policing and security operation will be in place until Friday, as European leaders meet in the capital as part of Ireland's EU Presidency. North Wall Quay will be closed to all traffic, including pedestrians, between Guild Street and New Wapping Street from 7am until Friday evening with diversions in place. Anyone travelling to or around Dublin city centre is being warned to plan their journeys and expect major and prolonged traffic disruption. A security cordon is in place around the Convention Centre, with barriers and no-parking restrictions. There will be additional restrictions around the Convention Centre and National Gallery of Ireland from tomorrow, including the closure of the Samuel Beckett Bridge from 8pm.

stories.title: Behind The Story: Kilkenny chaos and tech honey trap
stories.summary: An influencer boxing event that ended in chaos at the weekend has sparked concern for the city's tourism reputation. The weekend event was organised by social media personality Harrison Sullivan, also known as HSTikkyTokky, who recently featured in Louis Theroux's Netflix documentary Inside the Manosphere. On this episode, Christoper Dunne, Digital Content Editor with the Kilkenny People explains how the controversial event ended up in Kilkenny. The event made headlines after disorder broke out following a confrontation during the event involving social media personality Mo Deen and controversial British activist Tommy Robinson. The disorder spread with several videos showing chaotic scenes inside and outside the event have been prominently shared on social media. One man was taken to hospital. "It was being live streamed on the platform Kick. At last count there were 1.8million viewers." Christoper explains that the venue, the Hub in Cillín Hill, issued a statement after the incident saying that they had a 'zero-tolerance’ policy towards violence, aggression or disorderly behaviour. However, he says concerns have been raised locally about for the impact on Kilkenny’s reputation. "The chair of the local Community Safety Partnership has called for a full garda investigation into the event."

stories.title: Why is there a space lab in Mullingar?
stories.summary: Analysis: The Co Westmeath lab is a sign of how Irish businesses are availing of an opportunity to become major players in Europe's New Space industry By Robert Conway-Kenny, European Space Agency Phi-Lab Ireland Ireland is on the brink of an exciting opportunity to become a significant player in Europe's rapidly expanding space industry. While the much publicised global semiconductor industry reached a value of €554 billion in 2024, the global space market quietly reached a value of €535 billion in 2025. With forecasts suggesting annual growth of 10 to 12% over the coming decade for the sector, the potential for Irish businesses, entrepreneurs and workers is enormous. Right now the space industry is undergoing a fundamental transformation, and Ireland is particularly well positioned to benefit from it. Traditionally, space manufacturing involved producing highly specialised individual components for satellites designed to operate for 10 to 15 years. But the maturation of the commercial space sector, often referred to as 'New Space', is changing everything. Instead of manufacturing one component for one satellite, companies may now be looking to produce thousands of components to support thousands of satellites, with new launches taking place annually across a widening number of launch providers globally. This represents a completely different manufacturing challenge, requiring advanced materials, innovative production techniques and more efficient manufacturing processes. It also creates opportunities for companies that may never previously have considered the space industry as a potential market.

stories.title: Ireland deliever on promises, but South Africa loom large
stories.summary: Amid the wider commentary surrounding the current state of Irish rugby, questions had been raised about how Ireland would rediscover their point of difference among the heavyweights of international rugby. There was plenty of talk in the build-up to the dominant win over Argentina about how Ireland intended to evolve. They would be fitter, demand higher standards of themselves and, crucially, use their skillset to find ways of beating teams capable of matching them physically up front. The most impressive aspect of Friday night's performance was that the team delivered on what they had promised. Argentina are exactly the type of opposition capable of causing Ireland problems. They have the physicality, attacking threat and unpredictability to disrupt the Irish game plan. Having beaten a newly-assembled British and Irish Lions squad in Dublin last year, this was always expected to be a tightly-contested encounter. Andy Farrell's side conceded early, with Argentina producing some clever attacking play that culminated in a cross-field kick exploiting Craig Casey on the edge of the defensive line. However, Ireland responded within minutes, with Hugo Keenan crossing for the first of his three tries. The move demonstrated their intention to move opposition defences around and use their handling ability to create opportunities. Robert Baloucoune provided the initial spark before releasing Mack Hansen, who produced an outrageous offload back infield for Keenan to finish.

stories.title: Johnny Depp says he owes his fans for their support
stories.summary: US actor Johnny Depp has said he owes his fans after they supported him "through thick and thin". Depp, 63, stars as the titular character in Ebenezer, a dark fantasy adaptation of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol. It marks his first live-action movie role since 2023 and first major return to the big screen since being at the heart of two public trials relating to his ex-wife, actress Amber Heard. In 2022, Depp sued Heard for defamation over a 2018 article she wrote in the Washington Post, which his lawyers said accused him of being an abuser. Jurors returned with a verdict in Depp’s favour. It came after Depp lost a lawsuit in the UK against News Group Newspapers - the owner of The Sun - over an article that called him a "wife beater". A judge ruled in 2020 that the content of the article was proven to be "substantially true".

stories.title: What the latest Dior campaign tells us about AI and fashion
stories.summary: The fashion industry seemed to embrace AI as a slick and buzzy innovation in recent years, albeit to mixed responses from fashion lovers and critics. Now, Sarah Magliocco writes, the tide is turning toward once again exalting 'human-made' creativity as a signpost for luxury. An anthropomorphic blueberry is screaming from a hospital bed at her doctor, a moustached pineapple in a white medical coat. Scroll. A cat in a ballgown is involved in a soap-opera-style love triangle with a tiger and a puma. Scroll. A group of toned, buxom fruits gather around an outdoor fireplace in a Love Island-esque showdown. Scroll. The deluge of aggressive cliffhangers and questionably misogynistic storylines makes way for a woman with a thick South Dublin accent, showing off a beauty product in her car. Her overly smooth appearance - a hyper-idealised, cartoonish beauty - and the occasional accent discrepancies reveal she is an AI creation, spat out by a machine-learning model. The majority of her videos are selling products with direct shoppable links. The comment section is a variable feast, from criticisms of AI to star-struck compliments of her beauty, which suggest the commenters believe her to be real. She represents the saturation of AI content on social media, much of it for entertainment and advertising purposes. AI has become well and truly woven into our daily lives, whether we want it to or not, and one aspect of this takeover is how we encounter and consume fashion and beauty. It's a progression from what Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg called the internet's first phase, focused on friends, family and people you know personally, and the second phase, dedicated to creators and influencers.

stories.title: Formal pay talks to resume at WRC, strike still planned
stories.summary: Formal talks on a public sector pay deal are to resume at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) today but, as of now, Thursday's planned public sector strike is still going ahead. It follows engagement by trade unions and Government representatives with an independent group led by Commission Chair Kevin Foley. Those discussions concluded in the early hours of this morning and a pathway back to formal talks has now been found. According to Government sources, the independent group identified a basis for resolving the issues referred to it. It is understood that when the parties meet at the WRC, it will be with a view to concluding negotiations and reaching a final agreement. Unions are considering what the Government has described as a "substantially improved" offer which would deliver pay increases of 10.5% in an agreement that would run until the early months of 2029.

stories.title: Trump Media swings to a quarterly profit
stories.summary: Trump Media & Technology Group swung to a third-quarter profit, while its revenue more than tripled from a year earlier, fueled by growth in its Truth API data-licensing business. Shares of the company rose about 1% in extended trading on Wall Street last night. Founded by US President Donald Trump and known for its Truth Social platform, Trump Media & Technology Group has increasingly sought to transform itself from a social media company into a broader technology and investment business. The company, which is in the process of merging with TAE Technologies in a pivot toward fusion energy, reiterated that the $6 billion deal would close in the current quarter. Earlier this year, Trump Media launched Truth API, describing it as a subscription-based data feed that provides licensed, low-latency access to publicly available Truth Social posts. Truth API and the Truth+ streaming platform together added $1.8 million in subscription revenue, accounting for the bulk of the company's revenue growth.

stories.title: Palin says he cannot walk without assistance after fall
stories.summary: Monty Python star Michael Palin has said he still cannot walk without assistance after falling and breaking his ribs at home. The actor, 83, had to cancel a number of events including his In The Philippines travel book tour after a fall in his bathroom in October left him with three broken ribs and a cracked pelvis. Palin shared a health update on Instagram which featured a photograph of him standing in a disabled road bay. He wrote: "It's now exactly a month since I thudded to my bathroom floor - returning from a pee at 3.30 in the morning. I still can’t walk without a zimmer. "The laughs are all on me. Zimmers were used in Monty Python when we wanted to play slow-moving elderly people. "Now I’m an elderly person for real, having to move very slowly as I have three broken ribs and a cracked pelvis. Bones take time to heal and I’m probably doomed to play this particular Python character for a few weeks more."

stories.title: Yoga and the art of slowing down at Carlow's Lisnavagh House
stories.summary: At a retreat in a historic Carlow country house, Deirdre Mullins surrendered her phone for a weekend of yoga, forest bathing, and life at a slower pace. Standing in the hallway of Lisnavagh House, I reluctantly handed over my mobile phone and watched it disappear into a wooden box. I had a mixture of panic and relief as I said goodbye to the little device that consumes so many hours of my day. "You're the first person to do this," Emily Bunbury, the woman of the house, told me. The first? I was surprised to learn that, despite offering guests the chance to surrender their phones during retreats, nobody had ever taken the opportunity. It had all started a week earlier, when an email landed in my inbox ahead of an autumn yoga retreat, inviting guests to hand over their mobile phones for their stay. My initial reaction was resistance. I had a million reasons why this wasn't practical. I needed my phone to take photographs, make notes for this article, listen to podcasts and audiobooks and stay in touch with the outside world. The list went on. But after several days of internal negotiations, I decided to give it a go.

stories.title: Inside the €5bn pay offer to public servants
stories.summary: Not only do they set wages for gardaí, doctors, teachers, nurses and thousands of others who work for the State, they are also used as a benchmark for many others across the economy. This year the Government will spend €100 billion on day-to-day expenditure - one-third, or €34bn, is on public sector pay. The last pay agreement, which ran from early 2024 to the middle of this year, granted public sector workers pay increases of 10.25% over two and a half years, at a cost of €3.6bn to the taxpayer. This time the Government has offered 10.5% at a cost of close on €5bn. We don't yet know if unions will recommend that workers accept it. The exact duration of any deal has not yet been agreed. But it could run for between two-and-a-half and three years. It would be likely to be backdated to July when the last agreement expired. The Government pencilled in €1.2bn for a public sector pay increase for next year but acknowledged that figure was just a starting point for negotiations.

stories.title: UniCredit to win EU nod for Commerzbank deal - sources
stories.summary: Italy's UniCredit is set to secure unconditional EU antitrust approval for its acquisition of Germany's second biggest bank Commerzbank, three people with direct knowledge of the matter said. The European Commission's approval underscores the regulatory push for cross-border financial mergers to create European champions. It will come on the heels of the European Central Bank's green light for the deal last month. UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel said yesterday that all the remaining regulatory approvals for UniCredit to take control of Commerzbank would come before the end of November, sooner than anticipated. The Commission, which is the EU competition enforcer, is due to decide on the deal by November 16. In a legal review of the takeover process, the EU watchdog initially had some concerns about whether Berlin's demand that the government keep two supervisory board seats at Commerzbank complied with EU laws, two of the people said. UniCredit has challenged the German government's demand and said it wants to appoint all 10 shareholder representatives on Commerzbank's 20-strong supervisory board.

stories.title: Timoney's stock continues to rise after breakout year
stories.summary: Just as it looked like Nick Timoney had cemented his place as Ireland's first-choice openside flanker, he may be needed elsewhere. The 31-year-old has had to be patient for his break in Test rugby, winning his first four Ireland caps across a period of four years, but he has forced his way impressively into Andy Farrell's plans in the last year, featuring in 11 of the last 12 games. On Friday night he was given the nod over Josh van der Flier in the seven shirt, and justified that selection with an all-action display from the back row, with only Tadhg Beirne - among the forwards - bettering his 10 carries and 12 tackles on the night, as Ireland hammered Argentina 42-12. His performance would certainly warrant another start, both this weekend against Fiji, and next week versus South Africa, but Sean Jansen's knee injury will have changed Farrell's plans, and cause a backrow reshuffle across the next fortnight. Timoney's Ulster team-mate David McCann has been called in to train with the squad this week, but it's unlikely the 26-year-old will jump to the head of the queue and start for Ireland this week. Farrell has plenty of options to work with, with Timoney, Cian Prendergast and the uncapped James McNabney all experienced at packing down at the base of the scrum, as well as at the flank.

stories.title: Chef Mark Moriarty: "You rarely get to reflect in this business"
stories.summary: It has been one hell of a year for chef, writer and podcaster, Mark Moriarty, with a new restaurant, a new business hub and a new baby. He talks to Donal O'Donoghue about why his passion for food will never outweigh the priority of family. Last month, Mark Moriarty undertook a literary hike across Dublin, from Chapters bookshop on the northside to Hodges Figgis on the south. It was a rare day off for the chef, writer, podcaster and TV host, so he decided to use those hours by signing his new cookbook, Everyday Delicious, in the capital’s bookshops. It was a job that needed doing, he says, plus he got to meet the booksellers and see the fruits of his labour. "You rarely get to reflect in this business because it’s just forward, forward, forward," he says, adding that at the end of his odyssey, he had a quick lunch (burger and chips), knocked off a radio interview and was home in time for dinner and help put his children to bed. "That was one of the best days of the year because the rest of the time has been absolute chaos". "One hell of a year" is how Moriarty describes 2026 in Everyday Delicious, a year that saw the 34-year-old open his own restaurant (Mark Moriarty Studio), which doubles up as a creative space for his TV shows, podcast, corporate events, photography and consultancy work, and where he employs a staff of eight.

stories.title: Emissions labels have 'small impact' on flight choices
stories.summary: Emissions labels displayed on airline search engines have only a small effect on flight choices – and lead many consumers to misunderstand the impact of flying on the environment, according to new research. The study by the ESRI's Behavioural Research Unit - funded by the Environmental Protection Agency - used a controlled experiment in which a nationally representative sample of 1,000 adults completed realistic online holiday-booking tasks. Participants were randomly assigned to booking websites that displayed either no emissions information, a label stating the flight’s estimated carbon emissions, or an additional label comparing emissions to other flights on the same route. The tested labels looked exactly like those currently in the market. The study found they have only small effects on flight choices and are widely misunderstood. Among participants who saw no climate information, 22% booked the flight with the lowest emissions. This was the same for those participants who saw labels stating the estimated carbon emissions. The figure increased slightly to 27% among those shown relative emissions labels.

stories.title: Irish captain Sheehan ruled out of Fiji game
stories.summary: Irish captain Dan Sheehan has been ruled out of the side's Nations Championship clash with Fiji on Saturday night. The 28-year-old was forced off for a HIA just before half-time in Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin and never returned to the action. The IRFU confirmed on Monday that Sheehan is undergoing a 12-day return-to-play protocol after suffering a concussion, which takes him out of commission for the meeting with the Fijians on Saturday. Leinster's Gus McCarthy has been called in to train with the squad this week, as has Ulster back row David McCann, who is drafted in to cover the absence of Sean Jansen. Connacht number 8 Jansen has been ruled out of the rest of the championship with a knee injury, picked up early in the second half of Saturday's win. The 27-year-old (below) made his Irish debut against Japan in the summer leg of the Nations Championship, but a knee injury saw him last just 44 minutes against Argentina with Josh van der Flier replacing him. Jansen will now return to his province for rehabilitation.

stories.title: Environmentalists facing escalating threats in Honduras
stories.summary: The dangers of standing up for land rights and the environment will be under the spotlight at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Wednesday. It comes amid growing calls for more recognition and protection for land and human rights defenders, who can face intimidation and violence in many parts of the world. Among the most dangerous countries is Honduras in Central America, where Kate Varley and cameraman Bram Verbeke travelled to meet some of the activists involved. He avoids public places, rarely stays in one location for long, and travels around in a bulletproof vehicle for his own safety. His extreme vigilance stems from his work defending farmers' rights in Honduras - work that has made him the target of repeated, credible death threats. "It is no secret that there is a strategy to assassinate the leadership of the agrarian platform, especially me," he tells us from the relative safety of a cooperative farm in the north of the country.

stories.title: FIFA must tackle transparency issues, says sports chief
stories.summary: Sponsors and fans will turn their back on FIFA if it is not fully transparent over the World Cup private investor plan and the Folarin Balogun case, a sports integrity chief has warned. To date FIFA has not committed to any external independent review of how its president Gianni Infantino developed the hugely-controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan, nor made any pledge to disclose information around the decision to suspend a one-match ban for United States striker Balogun during last summer's World Cup after US President Donald Trump called Infantino asking for a review. Emanuel Macedo de Medeiros, the co-founder and global chief executive of the Sport Integrity Global Alliance (SIGA), believes even if FIFA can withstand pressure to examine the facts from individual FIFA Council members, national associations and leagues, there will ultimately be external consequences. "The eyes of the world are on FIFA and the way this situation will be addressed and resolved," Medeiros said. "Yes, the sponsors have been silent. We have not heard the sponsors expressing themselves as they did during the FIFAgate (scandal) back in 2015. "But I would not confuse silence with apathy or indifference. I would not underestimate that, because every executive, every CEO of every big brand responds to somebody. They are accountable to their consumers.

stories.title: Thousands of books once banned by State to go on view
stories.summary: A collection of 12,000 books that were once banned by the State is to be transferred to the National Archives and made available for public viewing. The books, which are currently housed in the Department of Justice, are being moved as part of the repeal of censorship laws. Among the collection are some well-known works by authors Edna O'Brien and Brendan Behan, along with thousands of other works that were once deemed indecent or obscene. The ledgers, which outline the individual reasons why each book was banned, will also be available for public viewing for the first time. The room housing the material is deep within the department, and outside visitors are rarely, if ever, allowed in. "This room houses a collection of materials that were banned under censorship legislation," says Dr Brian Hughes, a lecturer in the Department of History at Mary Immaculate College.

stories.title: Carrick on the brink at Man United amid club review
stories.summary: Michael Carrick's days as Manchester United head coach appear to be numbered as the club reviews his position and considers alternatives. The Red Devils will spend the international break in the relegation zone after failing to add to August’s solitary Premier League win against Ipswich in Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. United languish in 18th spot and are reviewing Carrick’s position as the club take stock during the international break. Reports suggest the club intend to replace the former midfielder following talks on Monday, although Old Trafford sources insisted no decision had been made that evening. United director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada seriously considered sacking Carrick a fortnight ago after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth compounded a calamitous 4-1 Champions League loss at Como. The club eventually decided to give the head coach and his players the opportunity to turn the situation around before the international break.

stories.title: FBI probing Nvidia CEO Huang over spy claims - Trump
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said the FBI was looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Mr Trump said he "was amazed" by allegations about Mr Huang, who is among the president's closest allies in Silicon Valley. He said he had spoken to the CEO, who told him that he had no idea that the woman was a spy. "I know the FBI is looking into it," Mr Trump said. "I think that he'll be in good shape," he added. Nvidia shares closed down more than 4% after the company's board launched an internal investigation into whether Mr Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The probe, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on 63-year-old Mr Huang's future, given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

stories.title: NFL: Bills battle their way to victory at the Vikings
stories.summary: James Cook III had 31 carries for 107 yards and a touchdown, and the Buffalo Bills outlasted the Minnesota Vikings for a 23-6 victory on Monday night in Minneapolis. Josh Allen completed 21 of 31 passes for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception for Buffalo (7-1). Tight end Keleki Latu caught Allen's lone scoring pass. Carson Wentz completed only eight of 25 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions for Minnesota (6-2), which has lost back-to-back games after starting the season with six consecutive wins. Justin Jefferson had three catches for 58 yards on 11 targets. Max Brosmer replaced Wentz at quarterback late in the fourth quarter and finished 6 of 7 for 58 yards. The game remained scoreless until late in the first quarter, when Buffalo inched to a 3-0 lead. Tyler Bass made a 39-yard field goal one play after the Vikings defense stuffed Cook in the backfield on third-and-2 from the Minnesota 19-yard line. The Vikings evened the score at 3-all with 4:02 remaining in the second quarter. Will Reichard connected from 43 yards as coach Kevin O'Connell opted not to go for a first down on fourth-and-1 from the Buffalo 25-yard line.

stories.title: Ukraine delegation meets US envoys ahead of Russia talks
stories.summary: Ukrainian negotiators met with US envoys and European and NATO representatives in Abu Dhabi ahead of the start of talks with Russia on ending more than four years of war. "The first meeting will be held with representatives of the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, NATO and the European Commission, joined by US Special Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner," Kyiv's chief negotiator Rustem Umerov said on social media. "We will align our positions and coordinate our steps ahead of the next stage of negotiations." Russian and Ukrainian officials are to meet for two days of US-brokered talks - their first since February - after President Donald Trump suggested last week that a broad peace deal was possible in their four-and-a-half-year war and could incorporate Europe's security. Headed again by Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky as chief negotiator, Russia's delegation will include Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov for the first time and senior military officer Yuri Zhigarlovsky. After meeting privately with Russian President Vladimir Putin's envoy last week at the White House, Mr Trump predicted that a peace deal could emerge soon.

stories.title: Brady quits role as Birmingham City minority owner
stories.summary: NFL legend Tom Brady has relinquished his minority share in Sky Bet Championship leaders Birmingham City after three years with the club. The seven-time Super Bowl winner bought a stake in the club as part of the 2023 takeover by the Knighthead group, headed by his friend and business partner Tom Wagner. But Brady has chosen to step away despite Blues moving to the top of the table two days ago with a 2-1 win over Swansea at St Andrew's. "Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years," the club said in a statement. "It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community." Birmingham have expressed big ambitions on and off the pitch. Wagner has indicated his desire to reach the Premier League, while plans are in place for a new 62,000-capacity stadium in the city.

stories.title: California billionaire tax defeated - US media projection
stories.summary: California voters have rejected a one-time tax on billionaires, US media projected, despite growing anger over global wealth disparity. The tax would have forced around 200 billionaires in the state to pay 5% of their total net worth, with the money largely dedicated to helping pay for healthcare. CNN and CBS News both projected that so-called Proposition 40 would not pass, nearly a week after voters cast ballots on whether to tax the billionaires. With the highest population of any US state, California is notoriously slow at counting votes. Prop 40 was one of a bevy of proposals put to voters in last week's midterm elections, which delivered large-scale victories across the nation for the Democratic Party, and handed a drubbing to President Donald Trump's Republicans. The proposal was unveiled to fanfare in California, a state that would be the world's fourth largest economy if it were a country, but one in which there is a yawning gulf between the haves and the have-nots.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth to face expected impeachment vote this week
stories.summary: A Republican politician has moved to impeach US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the war in Iran, setting up a potentially explosive vote in Congress just days after President Donald Trump's party suffered a crushing midterm defeat. Kentucky congressman Thomas Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment accusing Mr Hegseth of illegally waging war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers as Pentagon chief. The Republican-controlled House could vote as early as Wednesday, with some politicians from Mr Trump's party signalling that they might join Democrats in supporting the charges. Impeachment would be a humiliating blow for Mr Hegseth and the Trump administration, but would not automatically remove him from office. That would require a trial and conviction by a two-thirds majority in the Senate -- a far higher hurdle, even after Democrats take control of the chamber in January. The impeachment push has gathered momentum since Tuesday's midterm elections, when Democrats swept both chambers of Congress amid widespread anger over the Iran war and soaring fuel prices.
